changes.finding: BC Builds: whether it meets the criteria cannot be confirmed without the share of units at least 20% below market. Non-residential space is 0.0% of area, under the 30% cap; ground must break within 12 to 18 months of the conditional land contribution letter.
The site is outside the transit-oriented areas; no provincial minimum height applies.

Community Housing Fund: does not meet the criteria: unit mix market 54.6%, rgi 22.7%, deep subsidy 22.7% is not 30/50/20. Its 2025 call did not proceed (February 2026), so no intake is open now; the program page says it will post when next seeking proposals (as of 22 Sep 2026).

A program for this kind of housing (a shelter): year-round, temporary (winter included) and extreme-weather shelters for anyone homeless or at risk of homelessness; a bed, meals, showers, laundry and support staff, free of charge; year-round shelters staffed 24 hours a day. It funds running a shelter, not building one: BC Housing pays the provider's eligible program costs (program staff, direct program expenses, property management and administration) on an operating budget negotiated with each provider. A project enters by a support services agreement with BC Housing; the framework names no open application, and extreme-weather shelters sit under a separate framework. Rents: none: funded services are free to the people who use them. Intake: not stated on the page read (23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.

A program for this kind of housing (a shelter): new shelter and temporary housing spaces for people who are unsheltered or living in encampments. It funds the operating cost of shelter and temporary housing sites in the communities the Province picks: program staff, direct program and support services, property management and administration, on a budget negotiated each year under agreements of up to three years. A project enters not by application: the Ministry of Housing, with BC Housing, picks priority communities and may sign a memorandum of understanding with the municipality; BC Housing then manages the procurement and chooses the non-profit operator. Ask the City whether it has one. Rents: at a temporary housing site a fixed rent at the maximum shelter component of income assistance, or a rent geared to income under the operator agreement; at a shelter site none. Intake: not an application program: communities are selected by the Province. Its criteria are not tested here.

Would be a program for this housing if it is Indigenous-led, or partnered with an Indigenous housing provider or Nation (not said on the option): affordable rental homes for Indigenous families, Elders, individuals and people with disabilities, on and off reserve; every home rent geared to income (fixed rents may be considered on reserve). It funds building the homes (the Province's funding programs page: "funding to build and to support the creation of" them). A project enters by BC Housing's request for proposals. No intake is open now (closed: no call is posted on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026)). Its homes are all rent geared to income; this option has 89 market-rent homes, which it would not carry. Its criteria are not tested here.

A program for this kind of housing (supportive housing): modular supportive housing for people who are homeless or at risk, with 24/7 on-site staff and supports. It funds nothing new: the program page says all its homes are completed and operational. A project enters it does not: the program is complete. No intake is open now (closed: all homes under the program are completed and operational (program page, read 23 Nov 2026)). Its criteria are not tested here.

80 beds need at least 368 m² of sleeping floor (4.6 m² a bed space) in at least 20 rooms of no more than 4 beds, by BC Housing's Shelter Design Guidelines; washrooms, dining, staff and program space come on top and are not sized here.

A program for this kind of housing (supportive housing): subsidized housing with 24/7 on-site support services for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, with a household income at or below the Housing Income Limits; adults first, families and youth where approved. It funds the whole capital cost, and afterwards an operating subsidy (approved expenses less revenue) and a support-services subsidy set by the approved staff schedule. A project enters through BC Housing rather than by a society's grant application: BC Housing works with municipalities and other landowners to secure a site, procures and builds the housing, and signs an operator agreement with a non-profit (three to five years, with an option for five more). The building is owned by the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation, the Province's land-holding company, in full; a non-profit operates the building. Rents: rent geared to income for every home; a resident on income assistance pays the maximum shelter component, and some projects set a flat rent. Intake: not stated on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.

Would be a program for this housing if it is for women, gender-diverse people and children leaving violence (not said on the option): housing with supports for women and their children who are at risk of, or have experienced, violence, in four streams: safe homes (stays of about 10 days), transition houses (about 30 days), second-stage housing (up to about 18 months) and long-term rental housing. It funds 1,500 new homes from 2018, and the service agreement each provider runs them under. A project enters by agreement with BC Housing: the framework names no application route, so ask BC Housing. The building is owned by the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation for the buildings and land created under the fund, leased to non-profit societies and co-operatives. Rents: 30% of income in second-stage and long-term rental housing, by BC Housing's rent scale; a resident on income assistance pays the maximum shelter component. Intake: not stated on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.

A program for this kind of housing (independent rental): a federal Crown corporation that brings financing, land and partnerships to affordable housing; it counts housing as affordable at no more than 30% of a household's before-tax income. It funds flexible financing, land and partnerships; no application terms were read. A project enters not stated on the page read; CMHC's Affordable Housing Fund page directs organizations to it. Intake: not stated on the page read (23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.

A program for this kind of housing (supportive housing): capital for emergency shelters, transitional housing and supportive housing that serve only people experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness, paired with wrap-around services; planning must show financial sustainability and services for at least five years after completion. It funds capital, alongside other funders: it cannot duplicate or displace other funding or exceed 100% of eligible costs. A project enters through the region's Community Entity, by its calls for proposals. Intake: by call for proposals from the Community Entity; none was read here. Its criteria are not tested here.

intake: closed 19 Dec 2025: the application portal is closed and all program funding is committed; CMHC directs organizations to Build Canada Homes; what: low-interest and forgivable loans and contributions for new affordable and community housing, shelters, transitional and supportive housing included; no new applications; construction start months after approval: 6.

A program for this kind of housing (independent rental): a City grant toward building non-market housing, for non-profit and co-op organizations building on their own land in Vancouver; stream 1 for self-sustaining projects that leverage senior-government funding, stream 2 for deeply affordable projects that rely on senior-government operating subsidies. It funds a capital grant, funded by the Empty Homes Tax. A project enters by the City's funding call, then Council approves each grant. No intake is open now (closed: no funding call is open at this time (program page, read 23 Nov 2026)). Its criteria are not tested here.
